sections.h2: Where in Clinton County are deeds filed?
sections.html:
Head for the courthouse at the county seat. The land records for Clinton County are kept by an office that combines the county clerk and the register of deeds, found at 100 E State Street, Suite 2500, with a phone line at 989-224-5270.

The doors are open on weekdays from eight until noon, then again from one until five. Staff ask that you walk in by 4:30 so a transaction is not rushed at closing time, and holiday schedules can shift. Passport services run from the same office by appointment only.

Do not expect the counter to help you write anything. Employees do not prepare or alter documents, do not give legal advice, and keep no blank deeds in stock. For a sale, a title company or attorney writes the deed and sends it over.

sections.h2: What recording a Clinton County deed costs
sections.html:
Thirty dollars flat, whatever the page count. The same figure covers a mortgage or a lis pendens, and the county's recording fees page lists it next to the add-ons below.

Charges the Clinton County office may add to a closing package
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 each
Release or assignment naming extra instruments$3 per extra instrument named
Stamp certifying a recorded paper$5
Photocopy$1 a page
Treasurer's tax certificate$5 for 25 descriptions, 20 cents more for each beyond

If you ask staff to search the index for you, the statutory rate is fifty cents per year covered, never less than $5.

sections.h2: Formatting mistakes that get a deed sent back
sections.html:
The county posts a sixteen-point checklist drawn from Michigan's recording statutes, and the office will look over a draft before you file it. Common reasons for rejection are an incorrect fee, no drafter named, names not typed under the signatures, a male grantor's marital status left out, and an unfinished notary block.

  • Page one needs a blank band 2.5 inches deep along its top, and a half-inch gutter elsewhere.
  • Use black ink, type at 10 points or larger, and white paper of at least 20-pound weight cut to letter or legal dimensions.
  • Open the first printed line with a statement naming the single event the paper records, such as a warranty deed. A paper that combines two events is refused.
  • List every party's street address, and put the drafter's name and address on the instrument.
  • Truncate any Social Security number to its final four digits.
  • Lift the legal description from the previous deed or a fresh survey instead of the abbreviated wording on an assessment notice.

A survivor deed must come with a certified death certificate, unless the certificate is already recorded and the deed cites its liber and page. A court order has to arrive as a certified copy bearing the court clerk's seal.

sections.h2: Who owes transfer tax on a Clinton County sale, and how much?
sections.html:
The seller does, in two layers. State layer: $3.75. County layer: 55 cents. Each is charged on every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one (MCL 207.504 and 207.523). Typically the title company deducts the tax from the seller's proceeds. Fifteen days after the deed is delivered is the statutory deadline, and the county treasurer is the collector.

  • Outside both taxes: any deed carrying less than $100 of value, and deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Outside the state tax only: foreclosure transfers and deeds in lieu, plus conveyances down a family line to a child or grandchild (MCL 207.526).
  • The county statute lists no family exemption of its own, so ask the register how the county layer is treated on a family transfer.

Print any exemption claim on the deed itself. If none appears, the clerk charges the tax at the window.

sections.h2: When a deed needs the treasurer's certificate
sections.html:
Any time the instrument is a warranty deed, a land contract, or a land contract assignment with a warranty clause. Under MCL 211.135 the register may not record those papers until the county treasurer has certified the parcel's tax status.

It looks back five years from the date on the instrument and flags tax liens or tax titles. A quitclaim without warranty covenants skips the step. For a seller who is behind on taxes, request a payoff letter from the Clinton County Treasurer early, so the balance can be paid at closing and the certificate comes back without a lien. Your title company can usually arrange the payoff from the seller's proceeds.

sections.h2: Clinton County housing at a glance
sections.html:
This is Lansing's northern commuter belt, with the cities of St. Johns and DeWitt and parts of Ovid, Lansing, East Lansing and Grand Ledge inside its lines. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $259,500, with $88,210 as the typical household income. Owners live in 82.2% of occupied homes, and renters pay $1,092 at the median.

The county has about 80,432 residents. Many stay put: 89.7% lived at the same address a year earlier, so a house for sale often draws buyers from outside the neighborhood rather than from next door. A house on a rural parcel may involve a private well and septic system, a legal description that spans acreage, and a survey, while a city lot usually comes with a short platted description. Either way, the register of deeds only needs the recorded instrument to meet the format list above.

sections.h2: What happens at closing when a Clinton County owner sells for cash?
sections.html:
The paperwork matches a financed sale. The closing agent submits the signed deed to the register with the $30 fee, adds a treasurer's certificate if the deed warrants title, and attaches either the transfer tax or the exemption wording.

Before you sign, ask who is ordering the certificate, whether the deed recites the full price or relies on a valuation affidavit, and what exemption, if any, is claimed. If you mail originals yourself, enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed comes back to you.

One more errand sits outside the register's counter. Within 45 days, the buyer sends the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit. A seller who claimed the principal residence exemption files to end it effective on the closing date.

A short checklist helps. Confirm the fee, confirm whether the treasurer's certificate is needed, check the exemption wording if the deed qualifies for one, and make sure every signer's printed name matches the notary block. If the office is closed for lunch or a holiday when your closing agent plans to file, move the filing to another day rather than rushing the package. A rushed filing is how a missing signature or wrong fee slips through and sends the deed back.

faqs.q: How much is the Clinton County filing fee for a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars, charged per document. Expect an extra $5 for the treasurer's certificate on a warranty deed, which covers up to 25 legal descriptions.

faqs.q: Who is liable for transfer tax when a house in St. Johns or DeWitt sells?
faqs.a: The seller. The statutes name the grantor as the liable party, and the title company usually withholds the tax from what the seller receives.

faqs.q: Will courthouse staff prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. They review drafts against the recording rules but leave the writing to an attorney, a lender or a title company.

faqs.q: Can I drop off a deed over the lunch hour?
faqs.a: Not in person. The office shuts from noon to one on weekdays. Phone 989-224-5270 to check holiday schedules.

faqs.q: Why did the register send my deed back?
faqs.a: The usual culprits are a wrong fee, a missing drafter name, signatures with no typed names beneath, a half-finished notary block, thin margins, or two recordable events on one paper.
